title: Canonical finite-stage inclusion tensor comparison
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the raw rational finite stages and their common-stage pair category $\mathcal C_X$ of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], with tensor and scalar comparisons of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For a finite coefficient subfield $E$ and $K,L$ in its rational constructible stage, let $i_E$ denote the recorded inclusion into $\mathcal C_X$. Define the canonical inclusion tensorator $\alpha_{E;K,L}:i_E(K\otimes L)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_EK\otimes i_EL$ as follows. Put $P=i_EK$, $Q=i_EL$ and $Z=E\vee E\le E$. Start from the common-stage tensor object, use its literal-object identification, its canonical isomorphism to stage $E$, and the recorded common-stage tensor comparison there; apply the rational tensor of the normalized reflexive scalar unit on $K,L$. The inverse of this composite is $\alpha_{E;K,L}$. Equivalently, it is the unique isomorphism heterogeneously equal to that composite inverse, retaining the literal pair-object transports. This specifies the entire isomorphism, including the identity coefficient-extension case.

proof.text: Unfold stageTensorFormula and take as witness the inverse of its displayed composite: the literal common-stage tensor-object isomorphism, isoToStage at E, and inclusion of commonStageTensorComparison followed by the rational tensor of the normalized reflexive scalar unit. Its endpoints are definitionally the required included tensor and common-stage tensor. The normalization holds by HEq.rfl.

For any other candidate, its normalization is heterogeneous equality to that same witness. Since both have the required isomorphism type, eq_of_heq gives equality to the witness. This proves uniqueness without any additional coherence lemma, also for reflexive coefficient extensions.
